subject_pin.repin_policy: This pin is the subject that was observed when the profile was authored, and the commit that lands the profile is necessarily a descendant of it: the bootstrap lane is generator-side and is not part of what a consumer binds, so the canonical body at this commit is complete. A repin must move main_commit, main_tree and owned_tree together to one exact merged skills-shared commit, and the checker resolves all three from main_commit, so a repin that moves the tree alone does not merely disagree with policy -- it does not resolve. Before any real consumer is bound under #528, repin to the exact merged commit that lands this file.

bootstrap_engine.why_not_a_new_engine: shared-skills-infra already ships an atomic, rollback-tested, receipt-emitting consumer bootstrap with a planted-defect suite. What was missing for this procedure was a profile naming it, not a second applier. A per-Skill applier writing per-Skill-named binding paths would give one consumer two control-plane authorities for the same question, which is the shadow-copy pattern CORE-LAW-001 and CORE-LAW-006 exist to refuse; it would also have to be kept in step with an engine it does not own, and would go stale silently because nothing compares them.

superseded_consumer_surface.why: One consumer, one binding authority. The engine's binding already content-binds every Skill in the closure, this one included; a second per-Skill binding file would answer the same question with bytes nothing reconciles.
The engine writes one requirements document per consumer, carrying the whole shared closure. A per-Skill requirements file makes the consumer's shared set readable in two places that can disagree.
Same reason, one level up: the engine's profile binding records the profile digest and its Skill closure, so a per-Skill profile file is a duplicate task-state owner.

Not generated at all, rather than seeded empty. A consumer creates these when it first enters those lanes; an empty generated directory for a lane nothing has entered reads as a lane that exists and is idle, which is the opposite of NOT_EXERCISED.

preconditions.why: shared-skills-infra's procedure classifies every Skill under registry.json before any consumer binding, and its engine enforces that step: an unregistered Skill has no admitted classification for a binding to point at. Admission is a person's act about what this organisation publishes as shared, so no Worker may record it, and no general directive to implement this issue authorises it. A safety review of this wave refused exactly that substitution.

preconditions.requirement: `repository_control_plane.REQUIRED_ORDER` admits `dual-track-code-review-loop` as its seventh entry, in the order this profile's `skills` array declares.
preconditions.why: The engine compares a profile's Skill closure to that constant by list equality, so a seven-Skill profile is refused before the registry is ever read. This is a separate gate from admission and is discharged by different work: admission is a decision, this is an edit in a lane this issue does not lease. It is recorded so that a reader who sees registry admission granted does not conclude the binding will now run.
